images.title: The river crossing puzzle
images.purpose: Show the puzzle scene: the lion, the sheep and the bundle of grass on one bank, and the boatman in his boat on the river.
images.composition: A wide river scene. Left bank at the far left with three things on it, the boat in the middle of the river, an empty right bank.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas holding a wide flat river scene, no shading. BACKGROUND: two soft blue-green hills (flat shapes) behind the river. RIVER: a wide flat blue band across the lower half of the canvas. LEFT BANK: a strip of land at the far left, above the water level, holding exactly 3 things left to right: a tied bundle of green #009E73 grass, a golden lion sitting, and a white woolly sheep standing. They are close together and clearly separate. BOAT: a small brown wooden boat on the water at the middle of the river, with exactly 1 person in it, the boatman, in a red shirt and an orange turban, holding one oar. The boat carries nothing else. RIGHT BANK: a strip of land at the far right, empty. Each name is written in small dark text just above what it names. Nothing else is drawn.

images.takeaway: The boatman has three things to take across the river, one at a time.
images.description: A river with the lion, the sheep and a bundle of grass on one bank, and the boatman in his boat.
images.context: Starting point is the chapter's river picture: the bundle of grass, the lion and the sheep on the left bank, and the boatman rowing in the middle of the river. The right bank is empty. The characters and the rule that the boat takes one at a time come from the puzzle.
images.teaching_notes: Ask: what happens if the lion and sheep are left alone? The sheep and the grass? Use the picture to list the three pairs before any move. Misconception M_RIVER_BOTH: the boat takes only one thing at a time.

image_decisions.why: The puzzle scene with all its characters sets up the rules that the whole concept builds on.
